summary: Intro discovery for Verdant Health exploring Redwood Private (VPC) deployment. Primary concerns: network topology, VPC peering vs private endpoint, cross-region constraints, data residency and KMS/HSM integration. Discussed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs for latency and cost, proposed next steps for peering diagram, SOC2 artifacts, and technical benchmark run.
topics: Dedicated capacity sizing and latency targets
KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/in transit
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on this, and with me is Samir, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Priya Kapoor: Good thanks, Priya here. We just want to get into the network side, so we did some reading but wanted to hear best practices.
[00:12] Miguel Alvarez: Yeah, miguel here, infra lead. Primary ask is we need private VPC connectivity, we can't go over the public internet for PHI workloads.
[00:20] Samir Patel: Totally, that's what Private deployment is for. Quick question: are you looking for VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (private endpoints), or a hybrid?
[00:28] Leah Brooks: Leah from security: we prefer not to have peering open long-term, we usually favor PrivateLink-type endpoints and stricter routing, plus audit logs.
[00:36] Daniel Park: Our infra is mostly in us-east-1, but we have some data in eu-west-1 for backups. Is multi-region supported for private?
[00:44] Alex Chen: Good question. Redwood Private supports regional deployments; you can run control plane in one region and private runtime in others. For cross-region access you can set up inter-VPC peering or use our managed replication; depends on latency needs and data residency.
[00:58] Miguel Alvarez: And what about egress IPs? We need a stable set for our allowlists to vendor firewalls.
[01:05] Samir Patel: We can provide NAT gateway egress IP ranges for dedicated pools; for PrivateLink you'll get interface endpoints in your VPC and then traffic doesn't egress to the public internet. If you use VPC peering, egress still follows your routing so you control NAT.
[01:18] Priya Kapoor: Is there a recommended pattern for KV cache and state? We have sensitive prefixes in memory and want to ensure in-transit is zero trust.
[01:26] Samir Patel: Right, so the runtime uses encrypted channels (mTLS). There was a doc i think we sent but to be clear the KV cache and model weights in the Private runtime are never transferred over the public net. We support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[01:38] Leah Brooks: KMS integration: can you integrate with AWS CloudHSM or do you need a managed KMS?
[01:44] Alex Chen: We support AWS KMS, and for higher compliance customers we can work with HSM integrations; that's part of the private/on-prem contract. We'll need to scope out the HSM details in the security deep-dive.
[01:54] Daniel Park: For PrivateLink, what's the approximate setup? Is there a component on our side?
[02:00] Samir Patel: You'll create VPC interface endpoints to our service name, then modify route tables for subnets that need access. We provide an endpoint service in your region and a short list of required permissions. It's a one-time setup per region.
[02:12] Miguel Alvarez: How about peering: any limits on routes or maximum route table sizes? Our network team is picky.
[02:18] Samir Patel: Peering is straightforward but depends on your CIDR plans. For large enterprise we recommend an AWS Transit Gateway or PrivateLink to avoid scaling route table rules; peering can get messy with lots of VPCs.
[02:29] Priya Kapoor: Are there latency numbers we can aim for? Our SLAs for product features are 200ms p95.
[02:35] Alex Chen: On Dedicated capacity in the same region we're regularly seeing 20-80ms p95 for short prompts, but it really depends on model size and sequence length. We'll send a benchmark plan to measure with your prompt set.
[02:46] Priya Kapoor: Costs: if we go dedicated vs hosted private what are the cost drivers?
[02:50] Alex Chen: Dedicated is fixed capacity — predictable monthly commit. Hosted is usage-based. For private you add networking and egress considerations; dedicated private often lowers per-token unit cost but has a commit. We'll include a sample cost model.
[03:02] Miguel Alvarez: We need to restrict outbound to only certain subnets and inspect TLS: will PrivateLink allow us to terminate?
[03:08] Samir Patel: With PrivateLink the TLS terminates at your endpoint interfaces; you control egress. If you need L7 inspection, you can terminate at your proxies. We'll provide the TLS cert fingerprints and key rotation notes.
[03:20] Leah Brooks: One more for compliance: audit logs and retention. How long do you keep request logs in the control plane? We need 12 months retention and ability to export to our SIEM.
[03:29] Alex Chen: We have configurable retention; by default hosted control plane keeps 90 days but for enterprise/private we can set 12 months and provide S3 export or syslog forwarding. We'll include the retention options in the security pack.
[03:40] Daniel Park: What's the onboarding timeline? We have a compliance window in Q2.
[03:44] Alex Chen: For Private VPC onboarding typically 4-8 weeks: initial network setup, security review, and benchmark testing. If you opt for Dedicated sizing and reserved capacity it may be a couple more weeks for provisioning.
[03:55] Priya Kapoor: Okay that's helpful. For the benchmark — do you need sample data or just prompts?
[03:59] Samir Patel: Prompts and sample payload sizes are enough to start. If you want semantic evals we can set up eval harness but no PHI in test data unless you sign the DPA addendum.
[04:12] Miguel Alvarez: Can we do peering to a transit gateway? yes/no?
[04:15] Samir Patel: Yes, we support Transit Gateway attachments for scale; that's the recommended architecture if you have many VPCs.
[04:21] Priya Kapoor: Any gotchas with cross-account peering? We run infra in a separate account.
[04:25] Alex Chen: Cross-account peering is fine but we typically recommend PrivateLink with resource-based policy to minimize IAM friction. We'll document both approaches.
[04:34] Daniel Park: About regions: if our primary region is us-east-1 and backups in eu-west-1, do you recommend separate runtimes?
[04:40] Samir Patel: Yes, separate runtime clusters per region is typical so data doesn't cross residency boundaries. If you must replicate, we can encrypt at rest and in transit and use customer-managed KMS keys in each region.
[04:52] Leah Brooks: Any automated fallback if a region becomes unavailable?
[04:55] Alex Chen: We support routing policies with failover to a compatible model or region, but for strict residency use-cases failover may be limited by policy; we'll capture your policy in rollout rules.
[05:07] Miguel Alvarez: OK, next steps?
[05:09] Alex Chen: Summarize: we'll send VPC peering/PrivateLink diagrams, SOC2 and security docs, and a benchmark plan. Samir will run through the test matrix. Leah you'll send a list of compliance artifacts and KMS/HSM preferences.
[05:22] Priya Kapoor: Good. Let's schedule the tech deep-dive for next week, preferably Wed or Thu.
[05:26] Alex Chen: I'll follow up with a calendar invite and include the pre-req network checklist. Thanks everyone.
[05:30] Conversation end.
